item.title: NEW: Kiteworks Urges Global Server Shutdown Over Imminent Attack Warning
item.description:
Headline: Kiteworks Urges Global Server Shutdown Over Imminent Attack Warning

Summary:
Secure file-sharing provider Kiteworks issued an unprecedented advisory on September 26, 2026, urging all customers to perform an emergency shutdown of their servers for six to nine hours. The recommendation followed 'credible threat intelligence' from law enforcement about a potential imminent cyberattack targeting a suspected zero-day vulnerability. The move, which affected on-premise and cloud-hosted systems globally, caused significant disruption and raised alarms due to the platform's use by government and large enterprises, and its predecessor's history with the Clop ransomware gang.

Severity: Critical

Categories: Vulnerability, Cyberattack, Threat Intelligence

Article Type: Advisory

Meta Description: Kiteworks issued an urgent advisory for customers to shut down all servers due to credible law enforcement intelligence about a potential imminent zero-day attack.

item.description:
Headline: FBI Investigates Breach of Jobs Portal; ShinyHunters Claims Data Theft

Summary:
The U.S. Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) has confirmed it is investigating a 'cybersecurity incident' involving its recruitment portal, FBIJobs.gov. The confirmation follows claims by the notorious cybercrime group ShinyHunters, which asserted it had stolen highly sensitive data on nearly all FBI agents and job applicants. The group alleges it exploited a zero-day vulnerability in Oracle's PeopleSoft platform, raising significant national security and counterintelligence concerns over the potential exposure of federal law enforcement personnel data.

item.title: NEW: Administrator of 'Rydox' Cybercrime Market Pleads Guilty in U.S.
item.description:
Headline: Administrator of 'Rydox' Cybercrime Market Pleads Guilty in U.S.

Summary:
Ardit Kutleshi, the 28-year-old creator and operator of the 'Rydox' cybercrime marketplace, has pleaded guilty to federal charges in the United States. The illicit platform facilitated the trade of stolen personally identifiable information (PII), credit card details, and malicious tools, processing over 7,600 transactions and generating hundreds of thousands of dollars. The guilty plea marks a significant victory for an international law enforcement effort that led to Kutleshi's arrest and the seizure of the marketplace's infrastructure.

item.description:
Headline: CISA: Ransomware Gangs Actively Exploiting Critical TeamCity RCE Flaw

Summary:
The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) has issued a heightened alert confirming that ransomware groups are actively exploiting CVE-2026-63077, a critical remote code execution vulnerability in JetBrains TeamCity servers. The flaw, rated CVSS 9.8, allows unauthenticated attackers to completely take over vulnerable CI/CD servers, creating a severe software supply chain risk. CISA had previously added the flaw to its KEV catalog, and this new warning underscores the urgency for organizations to patch their systems immediately.

Severity: Critical

Headline: Gyazo Screenshot Service Breach Exposes 23.6M User Records

Summary:
Helpfeel, the Japanese company behind the Gyazo screenshot-sharing service, has disclosed a major data breach affecting 23.62 million users. Attackers exploited a server vulnerability on September 11, 2026, to steal a database containing user records with names, email addresses, and hashed passwords. Critically, the breach also exposed metadata for 490 million images, including identifiers that could allow attackers to reconstruct URLs and view potentially private screenshots. All users are urged to change their passwords.

item.title: NEW: Critical WordPress Core Flaw (CVE-2026-87902) Exploited Within Hours
item.description:
Headline: Critical WordPress Core Flaw (CVE-2026-87902) Exploited Within Hours

Summary:
A critical path traversal vulnerability in WordPress Core, tracked as CVE-2026-87902, is being actively and widely exploited just hours after a patch was released in version 7.1.2. The flaw, with a CVSS score of 9.2, allows an unauthenticated attacker to achieve Local File Inclusion (LFI) and, under certain conditions, full Remote Code Execution (RCE). The vulnerability affects a vast range of WordPress versions from 4.7.0 to 7.1.1, creating an enormous attack surface that threat actors are rapidly targeting.

Severity: Critical

item.description:
Headline: Critical WordPress Path Traversal Flaw Actively Exploited (CVE-2026-87902)

Summary:
A critical, unauthenticated path traversal vulnerability in WordPress Core, tracked as CVE-2026-87902 (CVSS 9.2), is being actively exploited in the wild. The flaw affects WordPress versions 4.7.0 through 7.1.1 and allows attackers to include local PHP files, which can lead to remote code execution (RCE) in certain configurations. Exploitation began just hours after disclosure, and all site owners are urged to update to version 7.1.2 or other patched versions immediately.

item.title: NEW: ShinyHunters Bypasses WAFs in Renewed Oracle PeopleSoft Attacks
item.description:
Headline: ShinyHunters Bypasses WAFs in Renewed Oracle PeopleSoft Attacks

Summary:
The threat actor group ShinyHunters (UNC6240) has resumed mass exploitation of a critical Oracle PeopleSoft vulnerability, CVE-2026-35273. The new campaign uses a URL-encoding trick to bypass Web Application Firewall (WAF) rules previously implemented as a mitigation. Google has notified over 100 organizations of their risk, with dozens already compromised. The attackers are deploying a new backdoor called SIDEEYE and using the legitimate remote management tool MeshCentral for persistence, expanding their targeting from universities to healthcare, technology, and government sectors.

Severity: Critical

Categories: Vulnerability, Threat Actor, Cyberattack

Article Type: Advisory

Reading Time: 5 minutes

Meta Description: Threat actor ShinyHunters is bypassing WAFs to exploit a critical Oracle PeopleSoft RCE (CVE-2022-21371), deploying a new backdoor called SIDEEYE. Patch now.

item.title: NEW: Microsoft Details Destructive Cloud Tactics of JADEPUFFER
item.description:
Headline: Microsoft Details Destructive Cloud Tactics of JADEPUFFER

Summary:
Microsoft has detailed a destructive cloud campaign in Microsoft Azure by the threat actor Storm-3168 (JADEPUFFER). This 'agentic ransomware' group used compromised service principals for automated attacks. After a 15-hour reconnaissance phase, the actor executed a destructive phase lasting just seven minutes, deleting storage accounts, an Azure Key Vault, and attempting to wipe recovery backups. The attack highlights a shift towards highly automated, rapid-destruction cloud attacks that aim to cripple victims and prevent recovery.

Severity: Critical

Categories: Cloud Security, Ransomware, Threat Actor

Article Type: Analysis

Reading Time: 5 minutes

Meta Description: Microsoft details a destructive, automated cloud attack in Azure by the JADEPUFFER (Storm-3168) group, which used compromised service principals.
